recipes.name: Tuscan Smoked Turkey-Bean Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can petite diced tomatoes, undrained
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place beans into a large bowl, fill the bowl with water, and cover the bowl with a cloth. Allow to soak overnight.

Drain and rinse beans; place into a large soup pot. Add turkey legs, onion, and bay leaves to the pot, cover with water, then bring to a boil over medium heat. Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer for 3 hours.
Remove bay leaves and discard. Remove turkey legs from broth, separate meat from the bones and tendons, and return meat to broth.
Stir in celery, carrots, diced tomatoes, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper; simmer until celery and carrots are tender, about 1 hour.
Serve soup in bowls and sprinkle each serving with about 1 teaspoon Parmesan cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Tuscan Smoked Turkey-Bean Soup
raw_recipe.description: An Italian-inspired turkey bean soup is made from scratch with dried beans that are soaked overnight, then slowly simmered to tenderness with smoked turkey legs, veggies, and Italian seasonings. You can make this in a slow cooker, too.

review.reviewBody:
awesome - added about 2 tsp. thyme and tarragon
Update: have made this 3 tims and doubled each time as my daughter and family love it. Freezes well.

I did not care for this. Although made according to the directions [exactly] 2 tablespoons of Italian seasoning is way too much and is the only thing you can taste. I don't know if the writer made a typo, but I suggest if you try to make this cut the seasoning way back.
 
I will make it again, but skip the seasoning altogether and use a bit of my favorites.

I made it tonight but didn't cook for 4 hours because I used 4 cans of white beans and added chicken broth instead of water. Cooked the turkey legs for 1 hour and then shredded them. Cooked the other veggies for 1 hour. Otherwise, followed the recipe almost exactly. Used only 1 T of Italian seasoning which to my mind (and my husband's) was enough. Next time, I'll add more turkey (only had 1 1/2 lbs to start with) and also will try a little tomato paste.

I am hestitant to try recipes that have few reviews, but this one sounded very good to me and I am so glad that I took the chance. My husband and I both loved this soup! Since I wanted to make it right away I didn't soak the beans overnight. Instead I rinsed the beans and covered with water and brought to a boil. I let them boil for 2 minutes and then turned off the heat and left them covered for 1 hr. I then strained the beans and added fresh water. I couldn't find "smoked" turkey legs, so I
bought the fresh legs that were available. I made a sauce out of Lea & Perrins white wine sauce for Chicken, a few drops of liquid smoke, and a pinch of Italian seasoning. We grilled the turkey legs on the bbq coated with the sauce first. After a about 20 minutes I added the legs to the beans. I also added one can of chicken broth and didn't use as much water. Will make this soup many times!

This is absolutely the best soup I have ever made. I only had one turkey leg, so I put in a chunk of turkey breast and a stick of andouille sausage. Also added 2 large cloves of garlic and used mostly chicken bone broth instead of water. Used 1 1/2 tbsp of Italian seasoning instead of 2 tbsp. Took about 1 tbsp of salt for my taste. Can't wait to eat it every night while it lasts.

After reading the reviews I agreed that some changes sounded like it could make the recipe better. I used 6 cups of chicken broth rather than the water. I used only 1 drumstick as it was plenty meaty. I used some garlic powder, thyme and red pepper flakes - I didn't measure them, I just sprinkled them in. And lastly, I noticed that the picture that is posted looks as though the broth is milky so I used a small carton of whipping cream at the end after everything was cooked. The soup was excellent and when my husband likes something, you know you've hit the jackpot!
Oh so good!!!! Had to sub tomatoes for potatoes due to acid reflux, then added spinach and heavy cream, no parmesan needed, it was divine. Hubby requested for it to be on permanent rotation.

I loved this soup! I used home made chicken stock to cook the beans in after they soaked in water overnight- I also used mixed beans- pinto and great northern. I also just used 1 smoked turkey leg and that was plenty! I also used rotel tomatoes, garlic powder and some red pepper flakes.I used somewhat less than 2 Tb. of italian seasoning- but I think this is what helps MAKE this soup! I think this is the best bean soup I have ever made!My husband agrees:) We do love our dried beans- I think this is so much better than using ham- saw the smoked turkey legs and wings at the store and bought them for either greens or beans. This recipe is awesome!! Thanks for posting!!
Oh so good!!!! Had to sub tomatoes for potatoes due to acid reflux, then added spinach and heavy cream, no parmesan needed, it was divine. Hubby requested for it to be on permanent rotation.

This is a wonderful heart-warming soup for a cold winter’s day! I added a tablespoon of “Better Than Bouillon” chicken base, a big tablespoon of minced garlic, and a bunch of kale for added greenness. My family loved it!

This was a very hearty soup! I used turkey sausage and added in some sliced little red potatoes along with the beans. I also added in some spinach and a splash of heavy cream! It was rich and delicious!

Everyone loved it - added the red pepper flakes, used two legs (serious carnivores here), added 4 cloves garlic fine chopped, used veg broth in lieu of water and added a cup or orzo last 20 minutes. Awesome with chopped fresh Italian parsley and the parm on top with crusty bread! Thank you for a great recipe.

I followed the recipe fairly close other than using chicken broth instead of water. I also did not have smoked turkey legs, so I used about 1.25lb of leftover (frozen) Thanksgiving turkey and added a few drops of liquid smoke. I cut the Italian seasoning in half, and was probably a bit heavy on the onion/celery/carrots. It came out well. Very enjoyable, and I will certainly try it again. I even froze a qt of it for a later dinner.

This is a new favorite. We had smoked turkey left after Thanksgiving and decided to give a smoked turkey soup a try. This looked simple and interesting. It is mind-blowingly good! This is our favorite soup. We plan to give jars to neighbors for Christmas.
Made recipe as written minus celery as I was out . Perfect basic foundation. Added Tabasco, someand additional herbs at the end.
What is the typical volume of broth? "Covering" in my case was 12 cups but I included the whole carcass not just the legs. This will impact the proportion of ingredients.

We cooked a turkey in our smoker. This was a perfect recipe for the broth we made from it and the leftover turkey. We like a little spice so we added crushed red pepper like others suggested. Served it with a salad and crusty bread.

This took a great deal of time, from the soaking of the beans to the cooking of the beans. It did turn out great and is worth the wait, if you’re willing to do it. I added some chopped jalapeño garnish on top of it at the end, to serve.

I soaked the small white beans all night then simmered them for eight hours and they were still a little firmer than I would have liked. I used the bones from yesterday's home smoked turkey and a light hand with the herbs and it was really good!

This is a great soup. I used a package of mixed beans, some garlic powder, and tarragon (with soup, I don't do a lot of exact measuring) in addition to the ingredients in the recipe. Will definitely make this again.
